narrative_spine: Danish immigrant patternmaker Charles E. Sorensen translates sketches into industrial systems: Piquette craft becomes Highland Park flow, Rouge foundry scale, and Willow Run wartime production. Repeatedly indispensable yet denied authorship, he is forced out, rebuilds identity through Willys and CESOR Farm, loses Caribbean holdings through Cuban expropriation, and is remembered through his family's 2026 Copenhagen return. Master metaphor: the pattern outlives the patternmaker.
industrial_spine: Patternmaking establishes sketch-to-casting translation; Highland Park assembly-line collaboration reduces Model T assembly from 12.5 hours to 93 minutes; Rouge monoblock V-8 requires a $50 million gamble and reaches 3,000 engines per day; Willow Run scales aircraft production to one B-24 every 63 minutes after early failure; Willys pivots Jeep from war machine to civilian product; CESOR Farm personalizes industrial demonstration; Fordism exports the pattern globally; Cuban expropriation ends Sorensen's private industrial empire.
character_spine: Sorensen moves from immigrant craftsman to enforcer, architect, regent, exile, self-mythologizer, and posthumously recovered builder. Henry Ford's vision and control produce symbiosis, ingratitude, and dependence on Bennett. Edsel Ford embodies the system's human cost and dies at 49. Peter E. Martin preserves collaborative authorship at Highland Park. Harry Bennett represents fear as rival power to production and is discarded when Ford's favor ends. The contemporary family moves from seekers to witnesses to custodians.
geopolitical_spine: The $5 day and labor system create mass society alongside speed-up, violence, UAW conflict, migration, and women's wartime work. WWII turns Willow Run into an Arsenal of Democracy and makes Ford succession a Washington concern. Ford plants export industrial logic worldwide, including to regimes the legacy would disown. Postwar capital moves through Cuba and the Virgin Islands; expropriation repeats authorship erasure at geopolitical scale. Reconstruction, Toyota's refinement, globalization, and worldwide assembly lines show Fordism surviving its authors.
visual_spine: Three-register grammar: archival record, present-day family/location verité, and consistent blueprint-derived pattern/casting graphics. Escalate Piquette wood and hand tools to Highland Park motion, Rouge fire and iron, and Willow Run aluminum scale; shift to Caribbean color, drained loss, then Nordic Copenhagen intimacy. Use family photographs, emigration records, factory footage, foundry reels, OWI and Ford Willow Run films, Willys films, CESOR materials, estate records, Lindbergh diaries, maps, chassis-flow diagrams, throughput arithmetic, and recurring hands-on-pattern imagery.
risks: Over-technical exposition can displace character; resolve every process beat into a human stake.
Over-heroization can erase collaborative authorship and Sorensen's role in workplace brutality.
Bennett conflict can be underplayed; retain production-versus-fear structure.
Cuba can feel like a disconnected epilogue; thread global Fordism and Caribbean capital strategy earlier.
Willow Run's 63-minute metric can flatten the story unless early failure and labor costs precede it.
Ford mythology can dominate; keep Ford inside Sorensen's perspective.
Obituaries and family remembrance may create false resolution; preserve partial, unresolved forgetting.
Archival availability and present-day access remain unverified.
open_questions: Which claims, dates, production figures, and collaborator attributions require archival verification?
What surviving CESOR Farm, Cuban estate, Virgin Islands estate, Helene, and Copenhagen materials are accessible?
Can Piquette, Highland Park, Rouge, and Willow Run present-day filming access be secured?
Which exact press items, Ford statements, internal memos, eyewitness accounts, and Sorensen memoir passages are available?
How should Soviet and German Fordism interest be documented without overextension?
What precise sequence and causes define Sorensen's 1944 forced exit?
What records document Cuban expropriation and the fate of each Caribbean holding?
